environment: Actual local HTTP listener, isolated PostgreSQL and synthetic provider MockTransport. No live product, buyer, license or sale.
checks: Verified license/email rotation immediately makes the old key return HTTP 401; new key lists four tools and successfully searches through actual /mcp.
Advancing the clock seven days before rotation leaves original redemption and expiration unchanged. Historical and current UTC-day counters are copied, and handshake/list calls remain uncharged.
A counter at 999 permits one remaining call after rotation, then returns HTTP 429. Another rotation preserves the exhausted 1000-call counter.
CSRF, ownership, refunded purchase and provider failure do not create a new key or revoke the active key.
Two requests verifying the same generation, synchronized at provider verification, produce exactly one successful rotation and one HTTP 409; only one active key remains.
An injected database failure after new insertion/revocation/counter copy rolls back the entire transaction, leaving the old active key, redemption and usage intact.
Rotation at the exact original 90-day expiry is rejected; it cannot extend the pass.
Stored rows, captured logs, later GETs and error responses do not reveal raw API keys or licenses.
reviewer: Independent coding agent. Synthetic checks do not establish a pre-sale or independent human sign-off.
remaining_work: HTTP /health and final Phase3 suite are checked separately. No deployment, public schedule or real buyer processing.
